title: Composition, namespaced ids and scope:global ADR conflict surfacing
description: Multiple blueprints may be applied to a single project. Blueprint-contributed docs are namespaced by the blueprint's slug so ids cannot collide across blueprints. A blueprint's ADR contributions may be tagged `scope: global`; two applied blueprints each contributing a `scope: global` ADR are a genuine conflict and `rcf blueprint add` surfaces both entries and refuses to write. Conflict-presentation ergonomics are prototype-unknown #1 (design brief); this US covers the first pass.
iWant: blueprint contributions to compose without id collisions, and for `scope: global` ADR conflicts to be surfaced with both sides visible before anything is written
soThat: composition never silently merges incompatible whole-project decisions

acceptanceCriteria.description: Blueprint-contributed doc ids are namespaced with the blueprint's slug so composition cannot collide on ids at the id layer
acceptanceCriteria.given: two blueprints `spa` and `rest` that both contribute a REQ, a US and an ADR
acceptanceCriteria.when: both are applied to the same project via `rcf blueprint add`
acceptanceCriteria.then: every contributed id carries the blueprint slug as its prefix (REQ/US: `spa-REQ-001`, `rest-REQ-001`) or as its kebab-suffix (ADR: `ADR-004-spa-theme`, `ADR-005-rest-versioning`); no two contributed ids across the two blueprints match

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint add <slug>` refuses when the new blueprint contributes a `scope: global` ADR on a topic already contributed by an applied blueprint
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with blueprint `alpha` already applied contributing an ADR tagged `scope: global` on topic `versioning`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `rcf blueprint add beta` runs and blueprint `beta` also contributes a `scope: global` ADR on `versioning`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verb exits non-zero, prints both ADR ids and their file paths, and the manifest is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conflict output includes both sides and names three resolution paths (pick, supersede, decline)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the output enumerates both ADRs (id, blueprint slug, path) and names the three resolution paths available to the operator (pick one and re-run with `--pick`, author a project-level superseding ADR, or decline the add)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Non-global TACs, ADRs, REQs, USs and FBSes are namespaced and cannot conflict
acceptanceCriteria.given: two blueprints each contributing a TAC on the same topic without `scope: global`
acceptanceCriteria.then: both TACs co-exist under distinct namespaced ids; no conflict is surfaced
